text:
Spotify’s October 21, 2026 [article](https://research.atspotify.com/2026/10/do-sequential-recommendation-benchmarks-require-higher-order-sequence-modelling) distinguishes low-rank **last-item** FMC/FMC+ from history-aware, count-based PCTM; it does not establish a recency-weighted low-rank hybrid or additive SASRec residual. The [FMC implementation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/spotify-research/sequential-capacity-probes/main/src/capacity_probes/models/fmc.py) uses separate source/target embeddings, s(i,j)=a_iᵀb_j, trained with softplus(−s_positive)+softplus(s_negative); FMC+ uses full-catalogue cross-entropy. In [PCTM code](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/spotify-research/sequential-capacity-probes/main/src/capacity_probes/models/pctm.py), weighted directed counts C_ij yield P(j|i)=(C_ij+τ/M)/(Σ_k C_ik+τ). Ranking-equivalent scores are Σ_l w_l log(1+MC_{h_l,j}/τ)+γ log((f_j+1)/(Σ_k f_k+M)). Count kernels support uniform, exponential and inverse-distance weights; normalized history kernels support exponential, inverse-distance, last-item and recent-head/older-tail mixtures.

The [official results](https://github.com/spotify-research/sequential-capacity-probes) give PCTM/SASRec+/eSASRec full-catalogue NDCG@10: Beauty .0635/.0537/.0524; Sports .0368/.0315/.0324; Toys .0738/.0575/.0533; ML-1M .1815/.1662/.1739; ML-20M .1431/.1806/.1969. These datasets and ranking conditions differ from the requested four-category sampled-candidate HR@10 benchmark. [FPMC and FOSSIL equations](https://arxiv.org/html/1609.09152): FPMC adds user preference p_uᵀq_j to a_lastᵀb_j; FOSSIL scores β_j+[|H\{j}|^(−α)Σ_{i∈H\{j}}P_i+Σ_k(η_k+η_k^u)P_{h_k}]ᵀQ_j. Thus additive multi-lag low-rank transitions have established precedent, although FOSSIL learns personalized lag weights rather than imposing exponential decay.

Proposed controls—not published findings: hold embeddings, loss and optimization fixed while comparing last-item, uniform and normalized exponential pooling; compare tied versus separate source/target tables and a parameter-matched wider SASRec; evaluate transition-only, SASRec-only and s=SASRec+λ·transition, including λ=0 and a frozen-branch validation-tuned blend. Keep history lengths, candidate sets and tuning budgets identical. Spotify explicitly leaves recency attribution and Transformer combinations for future controlled experiments.
